summary.headline: Admach FY26 revenue rose 29% to INR68.91 crore and PAT 59% to INR10.01 crore, but H2 margins fell to about 15% and operating cash flow was negative.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue from operations of INR68.91 crore (up 29% YoY), EBITDA of INR13.69 crore and PAT of INR10.01 crore (up 59%), with an order book of about INR65 crore. Gross margin reportedly fell from 33% to 29% half-on-half and EBITDA margin declined, which management attributed to project mix and new backward-integration machines still being commissioned. Receivables rose sharply (about INR18 crore to INR31 crore YoY) because of customer-held deliveries and export shipping delays, and operating cash flow was negative. Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin above 20% and working capital days of about 75.

financial_highlights.metric: Current tax rate in H2 FY26 (per analyst computation from filing)
financial_highlights.value: about 9.5% (current tax INR53 lakh on PBT about INR6 crore)
financial_highlights.change: vs about 25% in prior periods per analyst

segments.name: Steel processing (long and flat products)
segments.commentary: Management said steel is about INR100 of revenue mix with INR70-75 from long products and 25-30% from flat products. Scope is post-rolling-mill finishing, inspection and packaging, plus billet conditioning with Braun Machinefabrik (Austria), where one line was supplied to Tata Steel.

segments.name: NDT / X-ray and defense
segments.commentary: Defense was described as about 5% of current revenue. Applications include X-ray inspection of assembled 155mm shells (exported to Brazil) and missile-body inspection systems supplied to Taiwan and Korea. Standard X-ray cabinets come in 160kV, 225kV, 320kV and 450kV variants.

segments.name: Nuclear
segments.commentary: Order from Nuclear Fuel Complex of about INR10 crore, to be executed by end-September 2026. Management expects four to eight similar projects, with technical offers submitted.

segments.name: Packaging and exports
segments.commentary: Admach exports to over 28 countries. Direct US export orders include six pipe-industry projects from a US company, due for dispatch in about one month. Export margins are said to be slightly higher.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin target above 20%, supported by in-house machining from new CNC capex, which management said would add 3-4% to margin in upcoming results.
Management expects FY27 working capital days of about 75 and says operating cash flow should turn positive in FY27.
Order book of INR65 crore expected to be executed by end-September 2026, with bigger orders expected within months.
Offers worth more than INR200 crore have been quoted, with a conversion rate of about 60-65%.

Management said FY27 revenue could exceed INR100 crore, and an INR200 crore revenue level is achievable at the current facility, with a fair assumption of about INR200 crore by FY28 (management said 'hopeful and confident').
Working capital need of INR20-30 crore is estimated to support INR200 crore of revenue.
Dividend under discussion with the team; no further capex is currently planned for FY27 unless it improves margin or overheads.
capex_capacity: New assembly and testing hall built last year. Management said current facility can support about INR200 crore revenue versus about INR70 crore now; land is already purchased for Unit 2 and Unit 3.

CNC laser cutting machine and CNC press brake arrived; all installed, and all except the CNC press brake are commissioned. One more machine to be commissioned in 8-15 days and two more due by July 2026.
In-house share of raw material and job work was 30% in-house and 70% outsourced; management said this flips to 70% in-house and 30% outsourced after the new machines.
Management said the H2 EBITDA dip was linked to these machines being commissioned in the last one or two months.
demand_pricing: Competition in nuclear is from Europe only; European vendors often partner with Admach in India to meet the 50% Make in India requirement.
Customers use customised payment terms per PO; standard terms are 20% advance, about 70% before shipment and about 10% after installation (retention).
Management said current order book is a mixed bag across packaging, defense, nuclear and steel, and defense is the fastest growing segment.
Management said a new bright-bar and super-finishing machine line is under execution, with no plan to enter hot-rolling equipment.
Shipping delays due to the Middle East war and container shortages at Bombay port held up some dispatches; management said routing via South Africa is under way.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin decline quarter-on-quarter and gross margin fall from 33% to 29%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new backward-integration machines were only partly started or under commissioning, and the Company Secretary attributed the decline to project mix, with one large steel project (Tata Steel) driving earlier profitability.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise from about INR18 crore to INR31 crore, and why is receivable days about 150-160?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said receivables reflect customised credit terms per PO, with 70-80% received after commissioning and 20% as performance guarantee; two or three projects are waiting on shipment, with payment due at Bombay port, and management expects collection within the first half of the next year.

qa_highlights.question: Can margin rebound to above 20% in FY27 and is there any risk from the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of the 20% EBITDA margin target, saying delays were not a stoppage and solutions exist for shipping via South Africa.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the H2 tax rate about 9% when the annual rate is 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said higher depreciation from new capex under the IT Act reduced the tax liability in H2. The analyst questioned this, noting H1 and H2 depreciation were similar, and management agreed to revert on it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order conversion and pipeline outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said offers worth more than INR200 crore have been quoted, with a 60-65% conversion rate, and the INR65 crore order book should be completed by end-September.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital cycle and cash flow position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said working capital needs are about 1.5-2 months of project cost on a five-month project, with a three-and-a-half to four-month average project duration. The CFO was negative because of working capital movements after listing, though the company holds healthy cash reserves.

risks_watch: Receivable days of about 150-160 and negative operating cash flow for FY26; watch collections in H1 FY27.
Management's inconsistent answers on the tax rate (9% vs 17%-25%) and a promised follow-up; watch the tax reconciliation.
Conversion of the Nuclear Fuel Complex follow-on orders (four to eight projects) and the 155mm shell orders, both guided to close in one to three months.
Delays from shipping disruption linked to the Middle East war and container availability.
No product or segment revenue split provided on the call (management said it would be shared with ORIM); defense is about 5% of revenue, so growth depends on steel and packaging.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and the 20% FY27 margin target, but evasive on specifics: it declined to name nuclear projects or give a product split, and it deferred the receivables, tax and cash flow questions.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue to pass INR100 crore (about +45% on FY26's INR68.91 crore, midpoint-style 100% was not stated; implied ~45%+), backed by a commissioned hall sized for INR200 crore, a INR65 crore order book to execute by Sep 2026, and INR200 crore+ of offers quoted at 60-65% conversion, though the new machines are still in trial and no quarterly split was given.
